# @unmango/remark-tdl-mermaid

A [remark](https://github.com/remarkjs/remark) plugin that draws a [TDL](https://github.com/UnstoppableMango/tdl) model, written in a code fence, as a Mermaid class diagram.

````markdown
```tdl mermaid
package shop

type Order {
  id: string
  lines: [LineItem]
}

type LineItem {
  sku: string
  quantity: int32
}
```
````

becomes the fence `tdl gen --target mermaid` writes for the same model:

````markdown
```mermaid
%% Code generated by tdl. DO NOT EDIT.
classDiagram
  ...
```
````

so a site that renders Mermaid, GitHub included, shows the diagram.

```shell
npm install --save-dev @unmango/remark-tdl-mermaid
```

```js
import { remark } from "remark";
import remarkTdlMermaid from "@unmango/remark-tdl-mermaid";

const file = await remark().use(remarkTdlMermaid).process(markdown);
```

## Fences

Only a fence whose language is `tdl` and whose meta holds the word `mermaid` is drawn; a plain `tdl` fence is left alone.

Each fence is one self-contained TDL file: it declares a `package`, and it imports nothing.
A fence with no `target mermaid` block gets an empty one, and a fence with its own block keeps it, so its directives (`service`, `rpc`, `stream`) reach the diagram.
Directives go in the fence's target block, never in the meta.

A fence that does not lower, or that the backend refuses, fails the file with the error at its line in the markdown.
A warning is a message on the file, at its line, and the diagram is still drawn.

## Options

- `tdl`: the `tdl` executable to run. By default, the one `@unmango/tdl` installed, found through `@unmango/tdl/resolve`; `tdl-gen-mermaid` must sit beside it, as it does in `@unmango/tdl`'s platform packages and in the Nix package.

ESM, for Node 22 or later and Bun.
